tagline: A two-sea province with a colorful old town, Samila Beach and its mermaid, the Nang Ngam street quarter, and the border trade city of Hat Yai
introHtml:
Songkhla is a big southern province on the Gulf of Thailand made up of two very different cities. Old-town Songkhla sits between a lake and the gulf, with Samila Beach and its golden mermaid statue being the image most people picture first. The old quarter along Nakhon Nok, Nakhon Nai, and Nang Ngam streets is packed with brightly painted Sino-Portuguese shophouses, old-school coffee shops, and street art that keeps people wandering and snapping photos all day.

The other side is Hat Yai, a trade and food hub that buzzes day and night, with night markets, malls, and a steady stream of visitors from Malaysia and Singapore. Songkhla eats well across the board: fresh seafood, bold southern dishes, Hat Yai-style dim sum for breakfast, and local sweets like tao kuan. People come to Songkhla to stroll the old town, eat seafood, and hit Hat Yai all in one trip.
bestTime: February–August, when the skies are clear for swimming and walking the old town; November–December brings heavy rain and strong winds

highlights.name: Samila Beach and the Mermaid
highlights.blurb: Songkhla's signature beach, marked by the golden mermaid statue and the cat-and-mouse sculptures. People sit in the breeze under the pines, take photos with the mermaid, and look out at Cat and Mouse islands offshore.

highlights.name: Nang Ngam old-town quarter
highlights.blurb: A district of brightly painted Sino-Portuguese shophouses along Nakhon Nok, Nakhon Nai, and Nang Ngam streets, with old coffee shops, long-running eateries, and street art to photograph throughout the area.

highlights.name: Hat Yai
highlights.blurb: A trade and food city that buzzes day and night, with Kim Yong Market, night markets, big malls, and late-night restaurants. It's a regular stop for Malaysian and Singaporean visitors who come to sightsee and shop.

highlights.name: Songkhla Lake
highlights.blurb: Thailand's largest brackish-water lake, with Koh Yo in the middle known for its seafood and local woven cloth. Eat lakeside while watching the Tinsulanonda Bridge stretch across the water.

highlights.name: Khao Tang Kuan and the lighthouse
highlights.blurb: A low hill in the old town that you climb for 360-degree views of Songkhla, the lake, and the gulf. There's an old chedi at the top and a naga staircase to walk up, making it a popular sunset spot.

highlights.name: Khlong Hae floating market and southern food
highlights.blurb: A canalside floating market near Hat Yai open Friday to Sunday evenings, with southern dishes, local sweets, and boats selling food along the water. It's where Hat Yai locals come to graze in the evening.

foodScene.name: Fresh seafood and lakeside fish
foodScene.note: With both the gulf and the lake at hand, there's shrimp, shellfish, crab, and fresh fish. Spots along Samila Beach and on Koh Yo boil, stir-fry, deep-fry, and steam it southern-bold, served with a sea view.

foodScene.name: Hat Yai dim sum
foodScene.note: A favorite Hat Yai breakfast. Dim sum shops open early with shumai, har gow, steamed buns, and Chinese tea, and they fill up before the sun is even up.

foodScene.name: Bold southern dishes
foodScene.note: Gaeng tai pla, khua kling, gaeng lueang, and southern khao yam are everywhere in town, hot and salty-spicy, eaten with steamed rice and fresh raw vegetables on the side.

foodScene.name: Tao kuan and Songkhla sweets
foodScene.note: Tao kuan is a local specialty of rice crackers, fried tofu, blanched vegetables, and boiled egg drizzled with palm-sugar sauce that's sweet with a salty edge. It's an evening snack that's hard to find outside Songkhla.

foodScene.name: Hat Yai fried chicken
foodScene.note: Hat Yai-style fried chicken, marinated and fried crisp, topped with fried shallots and eaten with sticky rice and dipping sauce. It's a local star that people buy to take home as a gift.

foodScene.name: Stewed beef and old-school coffee
foodScene.note: Old shops in the old town make clear-broth stewed beef eaten with bread or rice, paired with strong traditional coffee. It's a classic Songkhla-style breakfast.

foodScene.name: Koh Yo seafood and chili dip
foodScene.note: Koh Yo, in the middle of the lake, is known for sea bass raised in floating pens. Lakeside spots make steamed fish, fried fish, and local chili dips, eaten with a view of the Tinsulanonda Bridge.

foodScene.name: Hat Yai street food and night markets
foodScene.note: The Hat Yai night market and Kim Yong Market are full of snacks, sweets, fruit, and fried bites. You can graze your way through from evening into the night.

attractions.name: Samila Beach
attractions.blurb: The city's signature beach with the mermaid statue and seaside pines, looking out at Cat and Mouse islands in the bay. It's where Songkhla locals sit in the breeze, take photos, and watch the sunset.

attractions.name: Songkhla old town
attractions.blurb: Nakhon Nok, Nakhon Nai, and Nang Ngam streets, with brightly painted Sino-Portuguese shophouses, coffee shops, long-running eateries, and street art to wander and photograph across the whole quarter.

attractions.name: Khao Tang Kuan
attractions.blurb: A hill in the old town that you climb for views of the city, the lake, and the gulf on all sides, with an old chedi and a naga staircase. It's a popular sunset spot.

attractions.name: Koh Yo and Tinsulanonda Bridge
attractions.blurb: An island in the middle of Songkhla Lake known for pen-raised sea bass, Koh Yo woven cloth, and lakeside restaurants. Drive across the Tinsulanonda Bridge that stretches over the lake.

attractions.name: Hat Yai and Kim Yong Market
attractions.blurb: A trade city with markets, malls, and food open late. Kim Yong Market sells dry goods and imported gifts, and it's a favorite shopping and eating stop for visitors.

attractions.name: Wat Khao Rup Chang and Khao Noi chedi
attractions.blurb: A temple on a hill in Songkhla town with a chedi and a city viewpoint. It's revered by locals and an easy stop for paying respects and taking in the view on the same trip as Khao Tang Kuan.

attractions.name: Songkhla National Museum
attractions.blurb: An old Chinese-style building in the heart of the old town displaying antiques and Songkhla's history. The building and its gardens make a nice spot to learn and take photos alongside the old quarter.

attractions.name: Ton Nga Chang Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A multi-tiered waterfall in the forest near Hat Yai with cool, clear water, trails up to each tier, and pools for a swim. It's a good cool-off stop on a day you want to escape the city.

itineraryIdeas: Songkhla 2D1N — old town, Samila Beach, Khao Tang Kuan
Songkhla old town and cafe run — Nang Ngam street, street art, traditional coffee
Hat Yai eat-and-shop day — dim sum, Kim Yong Market, night market
Songkhla sea and lake — Samila Beach, Koh Yo, Tinsulanonda Bridge
Songkhla–Phatthalung — loop the Songkhla Lake and see two towns
Hat Yai–Satun — head to the far south and on to the Andaman at Koh Lipe
